mainTopic: End of the aggadic passage on the זוהמא (spiritual contamination) from the נחש; then a new משנה on opening a barrel on שבת: breaking a חבית for גרוגרות, piercing a מגופה, and smearing wax. The גמרא opens with רבי אושעיא's limitation.
overview: The amud opens by finishing an aggadic passage about the זוהמא, a spiritual contamination the נחש put into חוה. Standing at הר סיני removed it from ישראל, and רב אשי explains that גרים were included through their מזל. רבי אבא בר כהנא disagrees and holds the זוהמא was already gone by the time of יעקב's sons. A new משנה then deals with opening containers on שבת. It covers breaking a barrel for dried figs, the dispute between רבי יהודה and חכמים over piercing the plug, the ban on smearing wax over a hole, and a story about רבן יוחנן בן זכאי. רבי אושעיא limits the barrel rule to pressed figs, which means our משנה follows רבי נחמיה, who forbids moving a utensil except for its designated use. The same split between רבנן and רבי נחמיה settles a contradiction between two ברייתות about fig baskets. רב ששת forbids piercing a barrel with a spear, because the person wants an opening, and רב הונא and רב חסדא argue over where the plug dispute applies. The amud ends with a ברייתא about new holes and רבה's rule that a one-way opening is only forbidden by a rabbinic גזירה; his explanation continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The נחש's contamination and how סיני removed it
steps.stepSummary: The נחש put a spiritual contamination into חוה. ישראל, who stood at הר סיני, lost it. The גוים, who did not stand there, kept it.
steps.simpleTranslation: When the נחש came upon חוה, it put contamination into her. ישראל, who stood at הר סיני, had their contamination stop. The גוים, who did not stand at הר סיני, did not have their contamination stop.
steps.whatsHappening: This amud begins in the middle of an aggadic statement. It explains where a spiritual flaw in mankind came from and how it was removed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea has two parts. First, the חטא of חוה brought a moral 'stain' into all humanity. Second, the experience of קבלת התורה at סיני cleansed it. So the dividing line is simple: whoever stood at סיני is cleansed, and whoever did not, is not.

keyTerms.meaning: Mount Sinai, where the תורה was given

steps.confusionAlert: This amud starts in the middle of a sentence. The opening words of this statement are on the previous part of the daf.

phrases.english: that the snake came upon Eve
it put contamination into her
Israel, who stood at Mount Sinai —
their contamination stopped

phrases.aramaic: גּוֹיִם שֶׁלֹּא עָמְדוּ עַל הַר סִינַי —
phrases.english: the nations, who did not stand at Mount Sinai —
their contamination did not stop

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁבָּא נָחָשׁ עַל חַוָּה הֵטִיל בָּהּ זוּהֲמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues an aggadic statement that began on the previous amud.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Standing at סיני removed the זוהמא from ישראל, but not from the גוים.

steps.title: What about גרים?
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בריה דרבא asks רב אשי how this works for גרים, who were not at סיני.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא the son of רבא said to רב אשי: What about converts?
steps.whatsHappening: A question is raised about the rule just stated. גרים were not at סיני, so did their contamination never stop?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule linked cleansing to being physically present at סיני. גרים seem to fall outside that, which would be a troubling result. The question pushes the rule to explain this case.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרָבָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Rav Acha son of Rava said to Rav Ashi:
What about converts?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the rule of step 1 against the case of גרים.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How does the זוהמא of גרים stop, if they were not at סיני?

steps.title: The מזל of the גרים was at סיני
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers that the גרים themselves were not there, but their מזל was. He proves it from a פסוק that includes 'whoever is not here.'
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Even though they themselves were not there, their guardian angels were there. As it is written: 'With whoever is here with us standing today before ה׳ our God, and with whoever is not here…'
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי answers the question. The גרים were present at סיני through their spiritual 'source,' their מזל, so they were cleansed too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer widens what 'standing at סיני' means: spiritual presence counts, not only being there in body. The פסוק in פרשת נצבים says the ברית was made even with 'those not here,' and the גמרא reads this as including future גרים.

keyTerms.meaning: Their מזל, meaning their guardian angel or spiritual source

steps.whatToRemember: According to this view, everyone in כלל ישראל was at סיני, including גרים through their מזל, and so everyone was cleansed of the זוהמא.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אַף עַל גַּב דְּאִינְהוּ לָא הֲווֹ,
phrases.english: He said to him: even though they were not there,
their guardian angels were there
as it is written: 'with whoever is here with us'
standing today before ה׳ our God
and with whoever is not here, etc.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אַף עַל גַּב דְּאִינְהוּ לָא הֲווֹ מַזָּלַיְיהוּ הֲווֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about גרים.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The מזל of the גרים was present at סיני, as the פסוק 'ואת אשר איננו פה' shows.

steps.title: רבי אבא בר כהנא: contamination ended with יעקב's sons
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes a disagreement. רבי אבא בר כהנא holds the זוהמא was removed after three generations of אבות, long before סיני.
steps.simpleTranslation: This disagrees with רבי אבא בר כהנא. For רבי אבא בר כהנא said: For three generations the contamination did not stop from our forefathers. אברהם fathered ישמעאל, יצחק fathered עשו, and יעקב fathered twelve tribes with no flaw at all.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that a different אמורא sees this differently. In his view the cleansing happened with the אבות, not at סיני.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof is from the children. אברהם still had a flawed son (ישמעאל), and so did יצחק (עשו). But all of יעקב's sons were perfect, which shows the זוהמא had already ended by then. That makes סיני unnecessary for removing it, which is why this view clashes with the previous one.

keyTerms.meaning: Tribes, here the sons of יעקב

steps.whatToRemember: There are two views on when the זוהמא ended. The first says at מתן תורה at סיני. רבי אבא בר כהנא says by the generation of יעקב's sons.

phrases.english: And this disagrees with Rabbi Abba bar Kahana
for Rabbi Abba bar Kahana said:
until three generations
the contamination did not stop from our forefathers
Avraham fathered Yishmael
Yitzchak fathered Esav
Yaakov fathered twelve tribes
in whom there was no flaw at all

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Presents a view that disagrees with steps 1–3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The זוהמא ended with יעקב's sons, before סיני.

steps.title: Breaking a barrel to get figs
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה allows breaking a חבית on שבת to eat the גרוגרות inside, as long as one does not intend to make a כלי.
steps.simpleTranslation: A person may break a barrel to eat dried figs from it, as long as he does not intend to make a vessel.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins with a new topic: opening containers on שבת. Its first rule permits smashing a barrel to get to the food.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Breaking a container to reach food is not considered destructive work or building. The one condition is that he must not shape a neat opening that would turn the barrel into a usable כלי, because making a כלי could fall under מכה בפטיש.

phrases.english: MISHNA: A person may break the barrel
to eat dried figs from it
provided he does not intend to make a vessel

steps.triggerLanguage: שׁוֹבֵר אָדָם אֶת הֶחָבִית לֶאֱכוֹל הֵימֶנָּה גְּרוֹגְרוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on an unrelated, practical topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: It is permitted to break a barrel for its food, without intending to make a כלי.

steps.title: Piercing the barrel's plug: a dispute
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה forbids piercing the מגופה, the plug of the barrel. חכמים allow it, but not through the side.
steps.simpleTranslation: One may not pierce the plug of a barrel; these are the words of רבי יהודה. חכמים permit it. But one may not pierce it from its side.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה brings a מחלוקת about making a hole in the plug to pour wine out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה sees a new hole in the plug as making a proper opening. חכמים permit it, but they add that one may not pierce 'from its side.' The גמרא later disputes what this means. According to רב הונא it means the side of the plug (step 22). According to רב חסדא it means the side of the barrel itself (step 25).

keyTerms.meaning: Plug or stopper of a barrel

phrases.english: And one may not pierce the plug of a barrel
the words of Rabbi Yehuda
And the Sages permit
but one may not pierce it from its side

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה with another way of opening a barrel.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה forbids piercing the plug. חכמים permit it, except from the side.

steps.title: No sealing a hole with wax
steps.stepSummary: If the plug already has a hole, one may not put wax on it, because spreading wax counts as ממרח.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if it was pierced, he may not put wax on it, because he is smoothing.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds a ban on sealing a hole by smearing wax over it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Spreading wax smooth is a form of ממחק, the מלאכה of smoothing. So even closing an existing hole is forbidden if it is done by smearing.

keyTerms.meaning: Smears or smooths, a form of ממחק

phrases.english: And if it was pierced
he may not put wax on it
because he is smoothing

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִם הָיְתָה נְקוּבָה לֹא יִתֵּן עָלֶיהָ שַׁעֲוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה: from making a hole to sealing one.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Smearing wax over a hole is forbidden because of ממרח.

steps.title: A story with רבן יוחנן בן זכאי in ערב
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה reports a case brought before רבן יוחנן בן זכאי in ערב. He was concerned the person might be חייב a חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה said: A case came before רבן יוחנן בן זכאי in ערב, and he said: I am concerned that he may be liable for a חטאת.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה supports a ruling of the משנה with a real case and a strict reaction from רבן יוחנן בן זכאי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying 'I worry he owes a חטאת' means the act might be a full Torah-level מלאכה, not just a rabbinic issue. The משנה does not spell out which act the story is about.

keyTerms.meaning: A sin-offering, brought for an unintentional Torah violation

steps.confusionAlert: Do not assume you know which ruling this story refers to. The משנה does not say, and the commentators discuss it.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda said:

phrases.aramaic: מַעֲשֶׂה בָּא לִפְנֵי רַבָּן יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּאי בַּעֲרָב,
phrases.english: A case came before Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai in Arav
and he said: I am concerned for him regarding a sin-offering

steps.triggerLanguage: מַעֲשֶׂה בָּא לִפְנֵי רַבָּן יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּאי בַּעֲרָב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a story to support a strict ruling in the משנה.
steps.raayaObject: That the act discussed is a serious, Torah-level prohibition
steps.raayaSupportSource: A case judged by רבן יוחנן בן זכאי in ערב

steps.title: רבי אושעיא: only for pressed figs
steps.stepSummary: רבי אושעיא limits the first rule of the משנה. Breaking the barrel is allowed only when the figs are דרוסות (pressed together), not when they are מפורדות (loose).
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: רבי אושעיא said: They only taught this about pressed figs, but not about separated figs.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins by narrowing the משנה's permission to break a barrel.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With pressed figs, one already needs a tool to pry them apart, so that same tool may also be used to break the barrel. With loose figs, no tool is needed for the figs, so handling a tool just to break the barrel is not allowed.

phrases.english: GEMARA: Rabbi Oshaya said:
they only taught this about pressed figs
but separated figs — no

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the first rule of the משנה (step 5).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Breaking the barrel is permitted only for pressed figs.

steps.title: Challenge: why not for loose figs?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions רבי אושעיא: is it really forbidden to break the barrel when the figs are loose?
steps.simpleTranslation: And for separated figs, is it not permitted?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a challenge against רבי אושעיא's limit. It is setting up the next move, which comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question doubts that loose figs should be any different. The משנה permits breaking a barrel without making that distinction, so the גמרא is preparing to bring a source or reason against רבי אושעיא.

phrases.english: And separated figs — not?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי אושעיא's limitation.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אושעיא's ruling that loose figs do not permit breaking the barrel
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Questions whether there is any real basis to forbid breaking the barrel for loose figs. The supporting argument continues next.

steps.title: A teaching that allows cutting off a barrel's top with a sword
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל allows cutting off the top of a wine barrel with a sword on שבת. This seems to contradict רבי אושעיא.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged him: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says that a person may bring a barrel of wine, cut off its top with a sword, and set it before the guests on שבת, and he need not worry.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא as proof that you may use a tool to open a barrel even when the tool has no other job to do. This attacks רבי אושעיא's limit to pressed figs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אושעיא said a tool may open the barrel only when the figs are pressed, because then the tool is needed for the figs anyway. In this ברייתא, the sword is used only to open the barrel and there are no figs at all. So it seems a tool may be used just for opening, even when the figs are loose.

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:

phrases.aramaic: מֵבִיא אָדָם אֶת הֶחָבִית שֶׁל יַיִן
phrases.english: A person may bring a barrel of wine
and cut off its top with a sword,
and place it before the guests on Shabbat
and he need not be concerned!
phrases.notes: He need not worry about moving the sword or about making a new vessel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source that backs up the question raised in step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אושעיא's limit of the משנה to pressed figs
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא allows using a sword only to open a barrel, so there should be no need for the figs to be pressed.

steps.title: The ברייתא follows רבנן, but our משנה follows רבי נחמיה
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא follows רבנן. Our משנה follows רבי נחמיה, who is stricter about moving utensils.
steps.simpleTranslation: That ברייתא follows the רבנן. Our משנה follows רבי נחמיה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי אושעיא. It says the ברייתא and our משנה follow two different opinions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבנן, a utensil may be moved for almost any need, so the sword may be used just to open the barrel. רבי נחמיה says a utensil may be moved only for its designated use. So in our משנה, the knife is allowed only because it is needed to separate pressed figs. Opening the barrel comes along with that use.
steps.confusionAlert: Here רבנן means the Sages who argue with רבי נחמיה. It does not mean the Sages who argued with רבי יהודה earlier about the plug.

phrases.english: That baraita is the Rabbis;
our mishna is Rabbi Nechemya.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigns each source to a different תנא (אוקימתא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא and the משנה follow the same opinion, so they contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא follows רבנן and the משנה follows רבי נחמיה, so there is no contradiction.

steps.title: Why not explain the משנה as loose figs according to רבנן?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי אושעיא made the משנה follow the minority view of רבי נחמיה. He could have said it speaks even of loose figs and follows רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: What forced רבי אושעיא to explain our משנה according to רבי נחמיה and only with pressed figs? Let him explain it as speaking of loose figs, following the רבנן!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions why רבי אושעיא chose the harder reading. The easier reading would follow the majority.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually we prefer to explain a משנה according to the majority, רבנן. Under רבנן, a tool may open a barrel even with loose figs, so the משנה could be read without any limit. The גמרא wants to know what pushed רבי אושעיא away from this simpler reading.

keyTerms.meaning: To explain or establish (a source as following a certain case or opinion)

phrases.english: And what forced Rabbi Oshaya
to establish the mishna according to Rabbi Nechemya and with pressed figs?
Let him establish it with loose figs, following the Rabbis!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reading that step 12 relied on.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אושעיא's choice to read the משנה as following רבי נחמיה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A reading that follows the majority and has no extra limit is simpler, so why not use it?

steps.title: רבא: the משנה's word 'dried figs' shows it means pressed figs
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that the משנה says גרוגרות and not just 'fruit'. This shows it speaks of pressed figs.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: The משנה itself was hard for him. Why does it say 'dried figs' in particular? It should have said 'fruit'! It must be teaching that it speaks of pressed figs.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the question. The wording of the משנה forced רבי אושעיא's reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If any fruit could be opened this way, the משנה would have said 'fruit' in general. Choosing גרוגרות points to a feature of dried figs: they are pressed together and need a tool to separate them. That need for the tool is what allows using it on the barrel, and that only works under רבי נחמיה.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי אושעיא reads the משנה as following רבי נחמיה. The tool may open the barrel only because it is already needed to separate pressed figs. The proof is the משנה's specific word גרוגרות.

phrases.english: Rava said:
The mishna was difficult for him:
Why does it specifically teach 'dried figs'?
Let it teach 'fruit'!
Rather, learn from this that it means pressed figs.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Proof from the exact wording of the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי אושעיא could have read the משנה as following רבנן with loose figs.
steps.terutzMaskana: The word גרוגרות shows the משנה speaks of pressed figs, which fits רבי נחמיה.

steps.title: Two teachings disagree about opening baskets of figs and dates
steps.stepSummary: One ברייתא allows untying, unbraiding, and cutting baskets of figs and dates. Another allows only untying.
steps.simpleTranslation: One ברייתא teaches: baskets of dried figs or dates may be untied, unbraided, and cut. Another ברייתא teaches: they may be untied, but not unbraided or cut!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets two ברייתות side by side that seem to contradict each other. It is setting up an answer that will again use רבי נחמיה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both ברייתות speak about the same baskets. The first allows cutting, which needs a knife. The second forbids cutting and unbraiding and allows only untying the knot by hand.

keyTerms.meaning: Woven wicker baskets used to hold fruit

phrases.english: It was taught in one baraita:
Baskets of dried figs and of dates —
one may untie, unbraid, and cut.
And it was taught in another baraita:

phrases.aramaic: מַתִּיר אֲבָל לֹא מַפְקִיעַ וְלֹא חוֹתֵךְ!
phrases.english: One may untie, but not unbraid and not cut!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a related topic, opening fruit containers on שבת.
steps.kashyaTarget: The two ברייתות about fruit baskets
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Two sources give opposite rulings for the same case.

steps.title: One ברייתא follows רבנן, the other follows רבי נחמיה
steps.stepSummary: The first ברייתא follows רבנן and the second follows רבי נחמיה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult: this one is the רבנן, and that one is רבי נחמיה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the contradiction by assigning each ברייתא to a different תנא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבנן allow using a knife for any need, so the basket may be cut open. רבי נחמיה forbids using a knife for something other than its normal job, so only untying by hand is allowed. This uses the same split as in step 12.

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
This one is the Rabbis,
that one is Rabbi Nechemya.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction of step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigns each source to a different תנא (תנאי היא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both ברייתות follow one opinion and truly contradict.
steps.terutzMaskana: The lenient ברייתא follows רבנן and the strict one follows רבי נחמיה.

steps.title: רבי נחמיה: utensils may be moved only for their own use
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי נחמיה's rule. Even a ladle, cloak, or knife may be moved only for its designated use.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: רבי נחמיה says, even a large spoon, even a cloak, and even a knife may be moved only for their designated use.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source for רבי נחמיה's strict view, which it relied on in the last answers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A knife is made for cutting food, not for cutting open baskets or barrels. So רבי נחמיה forbids using a knife to cut a basket. This is why the strict ברייתא follows him. It is also why רבי אושעיא, reading our משנה according to רבי נחמיה, limits it to pressed figs, where the tool is needed for the figs themselves.

keyTerms.meaning: For the sake of their designated use

steps.whyThisMatters: This rule of רבי נחמיה is the key that explains both רבי אושעיא's limit on the משנה and the contradiction between the ברייתות.

phrases.english: As it was taught: Rabbi Nechemya says:

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ תַּרְווֹד וַאֲפִילּוּ טַלִּית וַאֲפִילּוּ סַכִּין —
phrases.english: Even a large spoon, and even a cloak, and even a knife —
may be moved only for the sake of their designated use.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the view of רבי נחמיה used in step 16.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי נחמיה forbids using a knife for something other than its normal job

steps.title: Is it allowed to pierce a barrel with a spear on שבת?
steps.stepSummary: Students ask רב ששת whether one may pierce a barrel with a spear on שבת. Does the person mean to make an opening, or only to show generosity?
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked רב ששת: may one pierce a barrel with a spear on שבת? Does he intend to make an opening, so it is forbidden? Or perhaps he intends to be generous, so it is allowed?
steps.whatsHappening: A new question is asked about piercing a barrel with a spear. The answer depends on what the person intends.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Making a real opening in a vessel counts as fixing a vessel, which is forbidden on שבת. But someone who stabs a barrel with a spear in front of guests may just be showing off his generosity by letting wine flow freely, with no wish to make a lasting opening. The question is which intention we assume.

phrases.english: They asked Rav Sheshet:
What is the law about piercing a barrel with a spear on Shabbat?
Does he intend to make an opening, so it is forbidden,
or perhaps:
he intends to show generosity, so it is permitted?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new question about opening barrels.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether piercing a barrel with a spear counts as making an opening (forbidden) or as an act of generosity (permitted)

steps.title: רב ששת: he intends to make an opening, so it is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת rules that the person intends to make an opening, so piercing the barrel is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: he intends to make an opening, so it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת answers the question. We assume the person wants an opening, so the act is forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב ששת assumes the person's goal is the opening itself, so the act counts as making a פתח, which is forbidden on שבת. Step 21 explains why we assume this: someone who only wanted to be generous would simply open the barrel the normal way.
steps.whatToRemember: Piercing a barrel with a spear on שבת is forbidden, because we assume the person intends to make an opening.

phrases.english: He said to them:
He intends to make an opening, and it is forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 18.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The person intends to make an opening, so piercing the barrel is forbidden.

steps.title: Challenge from רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's sword case
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב ששת. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל allows cutting off the top of a wine barrel with a sword on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: They raised an objection: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says, a person may bring a barrel of wine and cut off its top with a sword.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב ששת's ruling with a ברייתא that seems to allow something similar to what he forbade.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב ששת said piercing a barrel with a spear is forbidden, because the person wants a real opening. But רבן שמעון בן גמליאל allows chopping off the whole top with a sword. That seems even more destructive, so why should piercing be worse?

phrases.aramaic: מֵיתִיבִי, רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: They raised an objection: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
A person may bring a barrel of wine
and cut off its top with a sword?
phrases.notes: This is permitted on שבת according to רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב ששת's ruling from step 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב ששת's ruling that piercing a barrel with a spear is forbidden.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If chopping off the entire top is allowed, piercing a small hole should be allowed too.

steps.title: Cutting off the top shows generosity, but piercing shows a real opening
steps.stepSummary: Cutting off the top is clearly done to show generosity. If the person piercing only wanted to be generous, he would simply open the barrel the normal way.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, he certainly intends to show generosity. Here, if it were true that he intends to show generosity, let him just open it normally.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב ששת by showing that the two cases reveal different intentions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Smashing off the whole top ruins the barrel, so the person is clearly making a show of generosity for his guests. Piercing a small hole is not a dramatic act. If he only wanted to be generous, he would just remove the plug. Choosing to pierce shows he wants that small opening, which counts as making a פתח.
steps.whatToRemember: The person's apparent intention decides it. A dramatic destructive act shows generosity and is permitted. A small, useful hole shows he wants an opening and is forbidden.

phrases.english: There, he certainly intends to show generosity;

phrases.aramaic: הָכָא — אִם אִיתָא דִּלְעַיִן יָפָה קָמִיכַּוֵּין —
phrases.english: here, if it were so that he intends to show generosity,
let him simply open it.
phrases.notes: He could remove the plug the normal way.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 20.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases (חילוק) based on what the action shows about intent.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Cutting off the top and piercing are the same kind of act, so both should be permitted.
steps.terutzMaskana: Cutting off the top shows generosity, while piercing shows he wants an opening. So piercing stays forbidden.

steps.title: רב הונא: the dispute is about piercing the top of the seal
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about piercing a barrel's seal. רב הונא says the dispute applies to the top of the seal, and everyone forbids piercing it from the side.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'One may not pierce the seal, etc.' רב הונא said: the dispute is about piercing on top, but from the side, everyone agrees it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to a new line of the משנה. רב הונא defines exactly where the dispute between רבי יהודה and the חכמים applies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה records a dispute about piercing the מגופה (the clay seal of a barrel). רב הונא limits the dispute to a hole on top. A hole in the side of the seal is forbidden by everyone, because it looks like a normal way of making a pouring spout.

keyTerms.meaning: The clay seal or plug of a barrel

phrases.english: One may not pierce a seal, etc.
phrases.notes: Quote from the משנה. רבי יהודה forbids it and the חכמים permit it.

phrases.english: Rav Huna said: The dispute is about piercing on top;

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל מִן הַצַּד — דִּבְרֵי הַכֹּל אָסוּר.
phrases.english: but from the side, everyone agrees it is forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new topic: the next phrase of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The dispute applies to the top of the seal. Piercing the side of the seal is forbidden by everyone.

steps.title: Support for רב הונא from the משנה's wording
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא's view fits the משנה's statement, 'He may not pierce it on its side.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And that is what the משנה teaches: 'He may not pierce it on its side.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that רב הונא's reading matches a line already in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה separately says not to pierce 'on its side.' According to רב הונא, that line means the side of the seal, which everyone forbids. So the wording of the משנה supports his view.

keyTerms.meaning: And that is what it teaches
He may not pierce it on its side

phrases.english: And that is what it teaches: 'He may not pierce it on its side.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings support from the משנה for רב הונא in step 22.
steps.raayaObject: רב הונא's claim that piercing the side of the seal is forbidden by everyone.

steps.title: רב חסדא: the dispute is about piercing the side
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא disagrees with רב הונא. The dispute is about the side of the seal, and piercing on top is permitted by everyone.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב חסדא said: the dispute is about the side, but on top, everyone agrees it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא presents a second opinion that flips רב הונא's reading of where the dispute applies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רב חסדא, piercing the top of the seal is permitted by everyone. רבי יהודה and the חכמים argue only about piercing its side. This is the exact opposite of רב הונא.

phrases.aramaic: וְרַב חִסְדָּא אָמַר: מַחֲלוֹקֶת מִן הַצַּד,
phrases.english: And Rav Chisda said: The dispute is about piercing from the side;

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל עַל גַּבָּהּ — דִּבְרֵי הַכֹּל מוּתָּר.
phrases.english: but on its top, everyone agrees it is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers an opinion opposite to רב הונא's in step 22.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The dispute applies to the side of the seal. Piercing the top is permitted by everyone.

steps.title: רב חסדא explains 'on its side' as the barrel's body
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא explains that the משנה's 'not on its side' refers to the barrel itself, not the seal.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the line that teaches 'He may not pierce it on its side' is talking about the body of the barrel.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows how רב חסדא deals with the line of the משנה that seemed to support רב הונא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: That line looked like it forbade piercing the side of the seal, which would contradict רב חסדא. He answers that it refers to piercing the side of the barrel itself. That is a different case, so his view still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: The body of the barrel itself

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the מגופה (the seal) and the חבית (the barrel). רב חסדא's whole answer depends on 'its side' meaning the barrel, not the seal.

phrases.english: And that which it teaches, 'He may not pierce it on its side' —
there it refers to the body of the barrel itself.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the implied difficulty for רב חסדא raised by step 23.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-reading the משנה's wording (it refers to a different object).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'On its side' means the side of the seal, which would go against רב חסדא.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'On its side' means the side of the barrel, which fits רב חסדא.

steps.title: ברייתא: no new hole, but adding to an old hole is debated
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules that one may not make a new hole on שבת. The תנא קמא allows widening an existing hole, while יש אומרים forbid it. Everyone agrees one may reopen an old hole.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבנן taught: One may not make a new hole on שבת. If he wants to add to an existing hole, he may add. Some say he may not add. All agree that one may pierce an old hole, even at the start.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with a three-level ruling about holes in vessels on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are three cases. A brand-new hole is forbidden. Widening an existing hole is debated: the תנא קמא permits it and the יש אומרים forbid it. Reopening an old, sealed hole is permitted by everyone, even לכתחילה.

keyTerms.meaning: An old, existing hole that was sealed

phrases.aramaic: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: אֵין נוֹקְבִין נֶקֶב חָדָשׁ בְּשַׁבָּת,
phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: One may not make a new hole on Shabbat;
and if he comes to add to an existing hole, he may add.
And some say: One may not add.
And all agree that one may pierce an old hole, even from the outset.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a related ברייתא about making holes on שבת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A new hole is forbidden. Adding to an existing hole is disputed. Reopening an old hole is permitted by everyone.

steps.title: Why should widening a hole differ from making a new one?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the תנא קמא. If a new hole is forbidden because it makes an opening, widening a hole also makes an opening.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the תנא קמא: what is the difference from a new hole, which is forbidden because he is making an opening? Adding also makes an opening!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the logic of the תנא קמא's position.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason a new hole is forbidden seems to be that it creates a usable opening. Widening a hole also improves the opening into something usable. So the same reason should forbid widening too.

keyTerms.meaning: The first, anonymous opinion in a ברייתא or משנה

phrases.aramaic: וְתַנָּא קַמָּא: מַאי שְׁנָא מִנֶּקֶב חָדָשׁ דְּלָא —
phrases.english: And the first tanna: what is different from a new hole, which is not permitted —
because he is making an opening?
Adding also makes an opening!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the תנא קמא of the ברייתא in step 26.
steps.kashyaTarget: The תנא קמא's ruling that adding to an existing hole is permitted.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The reason that forbids a new hole (making an opening) applies equally to widening one.

steps.title: רבה: a one-way opening is only rabbinically forbidden
steps.stepSummary: רבה explains that by Torah law, an opening not made both to put in and take out is not an opening. The חכמים forbade it only because of a chicken coop's vent. Since nobody widens a hole in a chicken coop, widening was not forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: By Torah law, any opening not made to bring in and take out is not an opening. The חכמים decreed against it because of a chicken coop, whose opening lets air in and heat out. So if he wants to add, he may add, because one certainly will not come to widen a hole in a chicken coop.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה answers the challenge by explaining that the ban on a new hole is only a rabbinic גזירה with a narrow reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A barrel hole only lets wine out, so by Torah law it is not a real פתח. The חכמים forbade it because it looks like a vent in a chicken coop, which works both ways (air in, heat out) and is a real פתח. People make new vents in a coop, but they do not widen existing ones. So the גזירה covers only new holes, and widening stays permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: To bring in and to take out

steps.whatToRemember: By Torah law, a real פתח must work in both directions. A hole in a barrel only lets things out, so it is forbidden only by a rabbinic גזירה based on the chicken coop. That גזירה does not cover widening, since nobody widens a hole in a coop.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets a key rule for the מלאכה of making an opening: it must serve both bringing in and taking out to be forbidden by Torah law.

phrases.english: Rabbah said: By Torah law,

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל פֶּתַח שֶׁאֵינוֹ עָשׂוּי לְהַכְנִיס וּלְהוֹצִיא —
phrases.english: any opening that is not made to bring in and to take out
is not an opening;

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבָּנַן הוּא דִּגְזוּר מִשּׁוּם לוּל שֶׁל תַּרְנְגוֹלִין,
phrases.english: and it is the Rabbis who decreed against it because of a chicken coop,
whose opening is made to let in air and to let out heat.
And so, if he comes to add, he may add,
because adding to a hole in a chicken coop
one certainly will not come to do.
phrases.notes: The sentence continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 27.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explaining the reason behind the rule: it is a rabbinic גזירה with a limited scope.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A new hole is forbidden by Torah law as making an opening, so widening should be forbidden too.
steps.terutzMaskana: A one-way hole is not a Torah-level opening. The rabbinic גזירה based on the chicken coop applies only to new holes, not to widening.
